title: add vpc control plane provisioning: subnets, endpoints, security groups, peering, dns (terraform + docs)
author: Ava Martinez
description:
Motivation: add first-class Terraform provisioning for Redwood Private control plane VPC resources so customers can spin up a managed control plane that integrates via VPC peering and private DNS. This PR implements opinionated defaults (CIDR layout, public/private subnets across AZs) and flexible toggles for attaching to an existing VPC, creating cross-account peering connections, and provisioning Route53 private hosted zones with conditional delegation.

Changes include: Terraform modules for VPC, subnets, NAT/gateway endpoints, security groups used by control-plane services, VPC peering resources and peering-accept/handshake helpers, Route53 private hosted zone + delegation records, ECR/S3/RDS interface/endpoint options, and example usage in terraform/aws/control-plane/examples. Also includes installer changes to automate peering handshake for customer accounts, a Helm values update to support new controlPlane.vpc.* fields, and documentation + upgrade/rollback guidance.

Checklist:
- [x] Terraform modules (vpc, subnets, endpoints, sg, peering, dns)
- [x] Example usage and variable documentation
- [x] Installer helper script for peering handshake + RBAC notes
- [x] Helm chart values for private mode
- [x] Integration tests (terraform plan/apply smoke in CI)
- [x] Docs: docs/private/control_plane_vpc.md with rollback guidance

Compatibility notes: by default the module creates a new VPC for the control plane. A flag control_plane.use_existing_vpc allows attaching to an existing VPC; when true the module validates subnets presence and will not touch route tables. Cross-account peering requires an explicit peering_role_arn and external account id; handshake is automated via installer/peering_handshake.sh but must be run by a user with permission to accept peering in the remote account.

Security: security groups are locked down to control-plane -> customer-data-plane communication over defined ports. IAM roles created for peering helper are minimal and documented. Reviewer requested further scoping (see comments) and tags for all resources were added.

Testing: CI runs terraform fmt, terraform validate, plan (with example vars), helm lint, and an opt-in infra integration job that runs apply/destroy in a sandbox account. Initial CI run failed terraform fmt and a missing provider alias; those were fixed in a follow-up commit and pipeline passed.

Release notes: See release_notes field.

Related: Linear ENG-4271 (VPC control plane provisioning), ENG-4310 (installer peering automation), SUP-112 (customer request for private DNS delegation).

review_comments: Liam Chen: Please scope the peering_role IAM policy to the minimum set of actions and limit resource ARNs where possible. Also add tags to all resources for cost center and environment.
Ava Martinez (author): Updated policy to only allow ec2:CreateVpcPeeringConnection, ec2:AcceptVpcPeeringConnection, ec2:DeleteVpcPeeringConnection and added tagging module to every resource. PTAL.
Priya Kapoor: We need a clear rollback path if the peering accept fails mid-install (network routes partially configured). Please add a note and automation to clean up partial resources.
Ava Martinez (author): Added rollback script and documentation section; installer now runs peering acceptance in a transaction-like flow and will attempt to remove route table entries on failure.

release_notes:
- Added Terraform modules to provision Redwood Private control plane VPC resources: VPC, subnets, NAT/Internet gateways, interface and gateway endpoints, security groups, and VPC peering.
- Route53 private hosted zone and conditional delegation records for customer-to-control-plane DNS resolution.
- Installer helper for automating cross-account peering handshake.
- Helm chart values for private control plane networking and example values file.
- Upgrade and rollback documentation for safe peering and DNS operations.
notes_for_ops: After merging: publish new terraform module version, update internal quickstart (redwood-quickstarts/private-aws) with example vars, and announce region availability. For customers using existing VPCs, confirm subnets and route table layout before running apply. Peering acceptance requires remote-account privileges and may incur eventual consistency delays in route propagation.
changelog_summary: Added Terraform provisioning for control-plane VPC and peering with docs and installer automation (ENG-4271, ENG-4310)
security_considerations: Security groups created are restrictive by default. Cross-account peering requires an opt-in role; IAM policy scope was tightened per review. All resources are tagged and logged. Customers should supply KMS keys for any data-plane encryption if required.
